active_ownership.title: [claim] Choose explicit Python function targets for test generation
active_ownership.body:
## Source contribution — estate-a219f250962c / estate_authority

Under Jacob's continuing estate execution mandate, this claims repeated explicit named targets on the native `targets` and `run` commands, starting from current main `e2285d68b2ea5eb2158c0a7e0d936ce5d56f8ff5`.

A developer who changes a module constant or a default binding currently cannot request tests for an unchanged affected function: two actual native CLI witnesses return zero targets and `no_changes`, and `--target` is unsupported. Proposed use: `python -m testpilot run --repo REPO --diff CHANGE.diff --target settings.py::accepts ...`, with the same repeatable option on `targets`.

The supplied target list selects exactly those functions, in caller order, deduplicated by source/function identity. Absence of the option preserves the existing automatic selector, prompts, output schema and behavior. Existing repository containment, Python source decoding and function/method discovery remain authoritative. Missing, ambiguous, test, outside-repository and non-Python targets refuse before test or model calls. Selected records retain only actual added lines; selecting an unchanged body does not manufacture changed-line coverage.

Explicit mode sends the exact loaded diff and current selected function source to planning, generation and repair. Optional explicit-only `selection` metadata records `mode`, exact `requested` specs, caller-selection `reason`, and `diff_text`. The existing `changed_functions` field remains the selected source-record list for compatibility. No dependency-completeness or live-model-quality claim is made.

Owned scope: new `testpilot/targets.py`; additive flags/dispatch in `testpilot/__main__.py`; narrow optional selection/context and report seams in `testpilot/loop.py`; an explicit-only selection/context notice in `testpilot/html_report.py`; focused new tests, `docs/EXPLICIT_TARGETS.md`, a narrow README link, and unique receiving evidence. Preserve the raw diff loader (#25), physical-line fences/patch (#22), `diff.py`, sandbox, model/client, generated-file allocation, #26 saved-run comparison, and the separately owned saved-test recheck.

Current native and GitHub ownership were reconciled before this claim. Isolated source: `/Users/me/hamon-testpilot-explicit-targets-a219f250962c`; this is a source contribution, not a resident worker/goal or an activation claim. Actual outgoing prompts plus real CLI → ScriptedModel → sandbox → patch receiving, exact default-path parity and independent root review precede source publication.

active_ownership.title: Preserve saved review artifacts when output staging fails
active_ownership.body:
## Scoped source contribution — estate-afe225d6c6be

A developer rerunning TestPilot into an existing `--out` directory can lose the last complete saved review if preparing or staging its replacement fails. The actual unmodified `write_outputs` truncates and writes the final patch, JSON, Markdown and HTML paths sequentially.

At native baseline `e1d87442eeecc8cf1b44ee3547849d5c1d030876`, a real 4096-byte file-size limit in an owned child reproduced two failures: an early patch write replaced the prior 237-byte patch with a truncated 4096-byte file; a later HTML failure had already replaced the earlier artifacts and truncated the previous complete HTML. An unrestricted changed-input control succeeded. Baseline receipt SHA-256: `cfd2d53bcff0d1a2654d3f4314aec994accf5b332a84393c6f47925ae7dedeaa`.

Fresh discovery main is `e2285d68b2ea5eb2158c0a7e0d936ce5d56f8ff5`. Its exact writer and incoming generation/diff changes will be received before edits; the original baseline keeps its actual source identity.

### Bounded behavior and source fence

Prepare all four output contents and stage complete files in the output filesystem before replacing a final artifact. A preparation, final-path admission or staging failure must preserve every existing final artifact and propagate the error. Reject observed non-regular or symbolic-link final targets before publication. Successful artifact bytes, names and returned path mapping remain compatible.

Final replacements occur only after staging succeeds. This scope does not promise an atomic four-file transaction, cross-process writer exclusion or power-loss recovery; a later replacement error must propagate honestly, with complete individually replaced files and the remaining publication limit documented.

Own only `testpilot/loop.py::write_outputs`, an optional new private output helper, focused tests, narrow output documentation and unique `docs/receiving/output-staging-afe225d6c6be/` evidence. Preserve current generation/fence/patch logic, HTML rendering, raw-diff transport, saved-test recheck, saved-run comparison #26, CLI dispatch, selector/model/sandbox/collector and their owners.

Engine execution authors the bounded implementation. Root owns all serialized GitHub writes and independent receiving/integration. Qualify with real isolated filesystem failures, changed-input success/byte controls, preparation/admission failures, cleanup and explicit late-replacement limits, current native suite and hosted checks. No model/provider call, real developer output directory or installed runtime is used.

active_ownership.title: Add saved-test recheck without model calls
active_ownership.body:
## Recheck the saved tests after a fix

A generation report already retains the exact proposed test files. This adds a usable `testpilot recheck` command that runs those bytes against a current checkout through the existing sandbox and generated-case collector, without invoking a model or replacing the original generation evidence.

```sh
python -m testpilot recheck \
  --repo /path/to/current-checkout \
  --report /path/to/original/report.json \
  --out /path/to/new-recheck-result
```

The result directory receives `recheck.json` and `recheck.md`. A previous recheck JSON can be reused. Exit status is 0 for current success, 1 for current failures or no retained passing cases, and 2 for admission/setup/output errors. `--python` preserves a selected project venv; `--timeout` uses the existing runner limit.

## Changes and ownership

- Add strict bounded saved-report admission, exact UTF-8 test-byte custody, and separate current results.
- Add an early CLI dispatch that returns before model construction.
- Add an opt-in `exact_files` sandbox mode for retained files. It creates missing tests with binary exclusive writes, accepts exact matching regular files without rewriting them, and preserves default generation behavior. This narrow scope extension follows a reproduced read-only 0444 failure; initial evidence is retained.
- Add 33 focused regression cases and the command guide in [docs/RECHECK.md](docs/RECHECK.md).

Ownership was recorded in [TestPilot #2](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/testpilot/issues/2#issuecomment-6060231013) and [HAMON #140](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/hamon/issues/140#issuecomment-6060236570). The exact accepted collector, model-timeout, HTML output and generation fence/patch contributions are preserved.

## Qualification and source custody

| Source | Actual qualification |
| --- | --- |
| R1 on `3e745e6` | 57 tests and 6 subtests passed; one existing optional coverage test skipped because coverage is absent. Ten real retained-report controls passed, including maintained buggy → fixed checkouts, exact applied read-only tests, conflicts, current existing-suite failures, timeout and selected project Python. |
| R2 on `e1d8744` | Only the new Python fixture changed to the project's existing `.pth` tooling-reuse pattern. The affected case passed. Three real-report controls preserved their outcomes against the exact accepted collector/HTML source. |
| Independent R2 review | Full source/CLI/sandbox/guide/test review accepted. Two actual CLI calls showed that forged historical “passed” metadata still gives current buggy exit 1 (three failures/one pass) and fixed exit 0 (four passes), with exact source, report and checkout preservation and zero model calls. |
| R3 composition on `aded01e` | All five owned product blobs are byte-identical to accepted R2. The only new upstream production change is PR22's exact `_FENCE`/`make_patch` logic. Static receiving verifies those generation-only definitions and the unchanged recheck import/dispatch boundary. No later full native rerun is claimed. |
| R4 on `e2285d68` | Preserve accepted PR27 raw diff input. The three recheck additions inverse-remove to the exact incoming CLI; the other four owned product blobs stay unchanged. Eight affected tests and twelve subtests pass, followed by an actual buggy/fixed retained-report pair with zero recheck model calls and exact source/report preservation. |

Native qualification used ordinary-user Linux Python 3.14.4 and pytest 9.0.2, with no dependency installation or live provider calls. The maintained original report came from the repository's real `calc_clamp` fixture and preserves its original bug result. Initial failures, bounded capacity stops and later corrections remain separately identified.

[Source-pinned records and commands](docs/receipts/recheck-68e476e98b77/README.md) retain the original and revised outcomes. Native R1/R2/R3 archives remain immutable. The earlier hosted 321-test/six-subtest success used the old `aded01e` merge fixture; the updated branch requires its own current-head CI. R4 native checks ran in an explicit temporary memory-backed root after the home-volume guard stopped.

The command requires a new result directory outside the checked source tree. Exact matching files are admitted as regular files, and conflict/symlink admission is rejected. The guide states the stable-path and partial-output limits; this adds no patch application or historical-success shortcut.

active_ownership.title: [claim] Compare two saved TestPilot runs without rerunning execution
active_ownership.body:
## Source contribution — estate-490fcd7c4056 / integration_review

Under Jacob's continuing execution mandate and HAMON #216, this claims an additive comparison of two saved TestPilot result reports at inspected main `e1d87442eeecc8cf1b44ee3547849d5c1d030876`.

A developer should be able to inspect recorded outcomes, source and target context, generated-file changes, diagnostics, coverage availability and recorded usage side by side without rerunning tests or calling a model. The comparison will offer both original JSON inputs as exact downloads and distinguish identical source/file identity, changed context and unavailable evidence. It will not infer unrecorded success or quality, recompute pricing, execute tests/models, apply patches or mutate a checkout.

Owned paths: new `testpilot/compare.py`, new `testpilot/compare_html.py`, an additive `compare` parser/early dispatch in `testpilot/__main__.py`, new `tests/test_compare.py` and `tests/test_compare_cli.py`, `docs/COMPARE.md`, narrow README usage, and unique `docs/receiving/saved-run-comparison-490fcd7c4056/` evidence. Proposed invocation: `python -m testpilot compare --before REPORT.json --after REPORT.json --out comparison.html`.

Current project issues/PRs, central HAMON #140 coordination and the native registry were inspected without finding a matching owner. Preserve #25 raw-diff transport, #22 generation/fence extraction, estate-68e476e98b77's saved-test recheck, and merged #17/#24 single-run report/writer behavior. Shared CLI additions will be composed with those owners while retaining all existing commands and diff-loader semantics.

Baseline uses real local ScriptedModel/pytest reports and the actual missing-command refusal. Implementation proceeds in an isolated owned directory; exact-source native CLI, malformed and mismatched reports, literal-text handling, keyboard/narrow browser behavior and exact-download receiving precede ordinary source integration. Root serializes this cohort's repository publication.
